channel.title: Japan AI Monitor
channel.description: AI monitoring of Japan's political, economic and security developments

item.title: Price hikes to hit Japanese households starting next month
item.description: Households will likely feel an increased financial burden, given that price hikes will also hit a wide range of food products.

item.title: Japan’s population fell 2.5% between 2020 and 2025, census shows
item.description: This was the third consecutive decline in the five-year survey that dates back to 1920.

item.title: Man held on suspicion of giving information to tokuryū criminal group
item.description: The arrest is believed to be the first by the Tokyo police of a suspected information source in connection with crimes involving tokuryū groups.

item.title: Trial of AI robot for visually impaired people shown in Tokyo
item.description: The robot is being developed by the National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation with the aim of eventually offering it as a rental service.

item.title: JIP adviser says coalition with LDP hinges on delivering results
item.description: The JIP joined forces with the LDP on the basis of 48 policy pledges, 60% of which have been set in motion, former JIP leader Nobuyuki Baba said.

item.title: Toyota’s car sales decline for seventh month as Chinese market favors EVs
item.description: Toyota- and Lexus-brand sales fell 23% in the world's biggest auto market in August on weak demand for gasoline and hybrid vehicles, Toyota has said.

item.title: University of Tokyo’s first female president vows to restore trust in scandal-hit school
item.description: Yuko Fujigaki, 64, told a news conference that she thinks being chosen to lead the 150-year-old institution "sends a big message to society."

item.title: Tokyo sets a new record with 34 straight days of rain
item.description: The rainy-day streak is the longest since the Japan Meteorological Agency began keeping records in 1886.

item.title: Thailand floods hit Thai Airways, Honda as disruption spreads
item.description: Thailand stepped up relief efforts as the severe flooding has widened the economic toll from days of torrential rain.

item.title: Japan defense chief again puts ‘nuclear taboo’ in spotlight
item.description: Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi says the country must possess the capabilities needed to counter threats directed at it.

item.title: Japanese volleyball player comes out as gay in rare case
item.description: Takahashi said his brother Ran, who is a hugely popular star with Japan's national volleyball team, helped him come to terms with his sexuality.

item.title: Reflationists? Who, us? Heirs to Abenomics insist it’s a thing of the past.
item.description: The current administration argues it's done with the policy prescription championed by Prime Minister Shinzo Abe and is now taking a different approach.

item.title: Japan’s Specified Skilled Worker visa holders rise to record numbers
item.description: The number of foreign workers in the country on the visa reached a total 444,256 at the end of June, up 13.8% from six months earlier.

item.title: Japan veers from rice shortage to glut, dealing blow to farmers
item.description: The oversupply is expected to weigh on prices until next year, adding to the insurmountable problems faced by many in an already-shrinking sector.

item.title: Swiss franc, Japanese yen Rise as DeepSeek News Boosts Safe Havens
item.description: The Yen and Swiss Franc were stronger against the dollar as investors sought safe havens after Chinese start-up DeepSeek’s new AI model hit U.S. tech stocks.
